newsitem.title: FRANCE: French DMC may break even in 97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: French DMC may break even in 97 - paper.

text.p: French textile group DMC will make a loss in 1996, but could return to break even in 1997, chairman Jacques Boubal said.

He said in an interview with weekly Investir magazine due to appear on Saturday, of the 145 million francs loss posted for the first half, 35 million was for exceptional charges, of which 29 million covered restructuring costs in printing.

"The effects of the current restructuring will not be felt before next year and the 1996 year will be in loss. We will not be in profit in 1997, but may be at break even," he said. A restructuring plan is expected to axe 1,500 jobs.

"There should be an improvement in results, that is sure, but the size of the improvement depends very much on the economic situation," he said, adding he had expected a recovery in printing in 1996 which had not turned up.

DMC has 90 percent of its production and 77 percent of sales in Europe. That was not tenable and had to change quickly and radically. The company had to reduce production capacity in countries where costs did not allow sufficient profitability.
Most of the job cuts would be in textile printing, particularly in Germany, he said.

He said it was "indispensable" for DMC to locate itself in growth markets. An alliance with the Hong Kong China Dyeing Works (CDW) "is very favourable" to the company's development and would allow it to expand in the southeast Asian peninsula.
He said he was not worried about if CDW exercised all its share warrants in DMC.
"If DMC wants to acquire an international dimension by association with foreign groups, one has to accept that its shareholding be open to international capital," he said.
